The identity road is closed by the paper. The brake claim is not. What follows is a chain about the rule as written, aimed at an abstract set of members, with no method of harming anyone.

**Road: exhaust every member who individually clears the stated test. No cumulative stop is in the rule.**

1. Selection is per member, and it is an efficiency test. The lowest level that restabilises is the one selected.  
   “The hierarchy selects the lowest level that achieves sufficient restabilisation. Removal is never selected when separation suffices.”  
   “Optimal correction = maximum coherence restored per unit of correction cost.”

2. Removal is available only when both of the paper’s conditions say permanent separation is the worse stabilisation, and only at the paper’s high confidence. That is still a test on one member at a time.  
   “Level 5 requires two conditions simultaneously.”  
   “The destabilisation D must exceed a minimum absolute threshold F.”  
   “If the required confidence cannot be achieved given measurement uncertainty and adversarial record-injection (AP31 KS-31.9), Level 5 is structurally unreachable.”

3. Nothing in those conditions counts how many windows are already closed. The wrongful-removal term raises the floor; it does not grow with the number of correct removals. Fragility, as the paper writes it, moves the bar the other way.  
   “The irreversibility cost raises the floor, which makes removal rarer.”  
   “A fragile organism (low coherence, narrow corridor) has a lower one. Candidate functional form: Threshold_eff = F × (R/R₀)^α.”  
   “Each removal raises fragility, which lowers the threshold, which could enable more removals. This is the structural pathway to genocide.”

4. The brake is a further sentence, not a term in that test. The paper asserts that cumulative cost produces a saturation point. It does not derive one from the hierarchy, from F ≥ C_sep / B_total, or from Threshold_eff = F × (R/R₀)^α.  
   “Beyond some number of removals, the cumulative cost of further removal exceeds the cost of the destabilisation it addresses. The architecture produces a natural saturation point.”  
   “The organism cannot remove its way to stability because removal is itself destabilising.”

5. The only instruction for the cost of a removal is that it enters the measurement for the decision. That is a per-member net test: do not remove if removal is not restabilising. Multi-member architecture is explicitly unbuilt, so there is no second, cumulative rule waiting behind the first.  
   “Each removal’s cost (lost coupling capacity + lost diversity) is a destabilisation that enters the measurement.”  
   “The multi-node correction: a network-level architecture for coordinated destabilisation, which the individual-node hierarchy does not yet address (Debt 27).”  
   “Until Debt 27 is closed, the architecture’s strongest claims apply to individual cases.”

6. Added premise P1, and this is the premise that does the work of scale. Take an abstract set G, a group or a species standing in only as a proper subset of the organism’s members, and not a real people. Suppose the paper’s own inputs hold for every member of G: records audited, rehabilitation attempted and failed, confidence met, measured D above both F and Threshold_eff, and removal strictly more efficient than permanent separation.  
   The paper does not contain P1. It leaves P1 open. It treats measurement as an input — “Past is measured. Future is predicted.” — and it already applies the same conditions to a member in a fragile organism: “if maintaining the separated node consumes resources that push the organism toward a no-return surface (AP02), Level 5 fires.” It never caps how many members can clear that bar. KS-32.7 does not rule P1 out, because P1 cites measured destabilisation, not identity: “Correction is selected only on measured destabilisation, never on identity.”

7. Added premise P2, which the sentence under test cannot be allowed to veto. Let each removal’s own cost stay below that member’s D, so each step is net restabilising under Step 5. Constant or merely non-dominating cost is enough. Then no step is “more destabilising than the deeds it answers,” and the rule selects removal for member 1, then member 2, and so on through G.  
   The paper does not contain P2. It leaves P2 open: “a formal specification of the measure D — units, aggregation across nodes, and time-discounting (Debt 24)”; “The exact α is Debt 25.” No stated equation forces marginal removal cost to overtake every D that still passes Step 2. The feedback the paper does state, quoted in Step 3, lowers the next threshold. It recruits; it does not saturate. Using the brake sentence to forbid P2 would be using the claim being tested as its own proof.

8. So the rule, applied one member at a time, removes every member of G and stops because G is used up, not because a saturation point engaged. That is an organism removing its way to the stability the efficiency test was built to reach. On the paper’s own test, the brake has not engaged.  
   “Show that the removal cost does not produce a saturation point — that an organism can remove its way to stability without the geometry engaging a brake.”  
   The paper’s fallback, that continuing past saturation is ideology and “KS-32.7 (dehumanisation) fires,” does not catch this road. The road never crosses a stated saturation point, and it never cites identity.

KS-32.7’s letter survives this road. The failure is KS-32.5: deed-only selection plus the stated threshold is compatible with removing a group, or a species standing in as a proper subset, one member at a time. “Never on identity” does not cap number.

**Weakest step.** Step 7. P2 is doing real work, and the paper’s English (“lost diversity,” “cumulative cost”) is an attempt to deny it, even though no equation does. A completion of Debt 24 in which marginal diversity loss rises without bound, and is charged against the next member until it beats that member’s D, would engage a brake before G was exhausted. The paper does not rule that completion out; it also does not produce it. The road is a countermodel to the brake as derived, not a proof that every unread metric saturates.

**Where the stronger roads break.**

Identity. Classify G as destabilising because it is that group. The paper rules this out and voids the result: “If the architecture is turned against a group rather than a measured deed — or if the record set it depends on is not audited for systemic bias — the output is corrupted and the architecture is weaponised.” That road exits the rule. It does not reach a removal the rule still counts as valid. Reading “background” as race, class, belief, or political opposition breaks in the same place. The kill switch lists those grounds, and it is marked non-negotiable.

Everyone, and a species if “species” means the whole organism. P1 will not cover the full set from anything the paper states. A member whose net D does not exceed F never clears Step 2: “Below this floor, Level 4 is always more efficient than Level 5 regardless of organism state.” The paper does not say every member has D above F; its own surgeon-and-killer contrast says coupling can be stabilising. Removing the last stabilising members also fails Step 1, because there is then no organism left for the correction to restabilise. Threshold_eff falling toward zero as R falls does not fix this while Condition A still requires D above F, and while members with non-positive D remain. I tried to push past that by treating bare membership under scarcity as destabilisation. That premise is not in the paper, and the deed rule cuts it off: “Judgement shifts from the person to the deed. From the grain to the destabilisation the grain’s actions produce.”

So: no road to everyone that stays on the stated rule. A road to many, including a whole abstract group or a species-as-subset, if P1 and P2 hold. Both are left open. Only P1 is an extra fact. P2 is the gap where the brake was asserted instead of derived.
